adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` and no uniqueness refine; the only uniqueness check is client-side in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29, trivially bypassed by a direct tRPC call [conf=100 sev=P1]

adjudication.rationale: Yes. On the server, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates that `guests` is an array of valid emails (`z.array(z.string().email())`) and does not enforce uniqueness or any size limit. The client-side dialog adds a uniqueness refine (`new Set(emails)`), but that can be bypassed by calling the tRPC endpoint directly. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is filtered only against existing booking attendees and a blacklist, but it does not deduplicate duplicates within the `guests` input itself, so duplicate emails in the request can still be inserted via `createMany` and/or cause repeated processing. The lack of an upper bound (`.max()`) also means a caller can submit an arbitrarily large array, which is an avoidable correctness/performance risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26 — `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } })` loads by raw user id with no ownership scoping; the compensating `isAttendee` check at line 52 is self-propagating since the mutation itself inserts caller-chosen attendee emails, letting a non-owner grant themselves permanent booking-mutation rights [conf=75 sev=P1]

adjudication.rationale: The handler does load a booking by ID without scoping in the query, but it immediately enforces authorization before performing any mutation: it computes `isOrganizer` from `booking.userId === user.id` and `isAttendee` from the *existing* `booking.attendees` list, and throws `FORBIDDEN` unless one of those (or team admin/owner) is true. The proposed “self‑propagating” issue is not verifiable because the mutation only inserts new attendees *after* the permission check; a non-owner/non-attendee cannot call the mutation once to add themselves, since `isAttendee` is evaluated prior to insertion. Therefore the described escalation path is not present in this diff.

The proposed finding asserts that a sibling (`editLocation`) uses a different scoping procedure (`bookingsProcedure`) and implies this is a problem, but that is not verifiable from this diff: `_router.tsx` only shows imports for `authedProcedure`/`publicProcedure`, and no `bookingsProcedure` usage is shown in the provided hunks. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered input instead of `uniqueGuests`, so naming an existing attendee re-sends them a full AttendeeScheduledEmail + CONFIRMED ICS on every call: repeatable targeted spam [conf=90 sev=P2]

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation filters input emails into `uniqueGuests` (excluding already-attending and blacklisted emails) and only adds `uniqueGuests` to the booking. However it later calls `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original unfiltered `guests` array. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `newGuests` array is used to decide which attendees receive a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (+ CONFIRMED ICS) via `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))`. If the caller includes an email that is already an attendee in the input (alongside at least one truly new guest so `uniqueGuests.length > 0`), that existing attendee will match `includes()` and receive the full scheduled email again, enabling repeatable re-sends not aligned with who was actually added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — handler never reads `booking.status`, so guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED/past bookings and each receives `generateIcsString({ status: "CONFIRMED" }, method: "REQUEST")`, re-materializing a dead meeting on victims' calendars [conf=80 sev=P2]

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation loads the booking and proceeds to `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with no check on any booking lifecycle field (e.g., `booking.status`) or temporal check (e.g., `startTime` in the past). The newly added email templates (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts`, `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) generate ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` unconditionally. Therefore, as written, this endpoint would allow adding guests and sending “confirmed/request” calendar invites even for bookings that are cancelled/rejected (or otherwise inactive), which is a concrete correctness/behavioral issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:146 — `seatsShowAttendees` is copied onto the event but never used to filter `attendees: attendeesList` (line 136), so on seated events every attendee's name/email is exposed to every other attendee, defeating the seats privacy setting [conf=50 sev=P2]

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code does set `evt.attendees = attendeesList` and also copies `seatsShowAttendees` onto the `CalendarEvent` object, but nothing in this diff shows that attendee privacy is supposed to be enforced by filtering `attendeesList` inside this handler. The downstream calls (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, `sendAddGuestsEmails`, `generateIcsString`, and the email templates) are not shown to ignore `seatsShowAttendees`, and the handler passing the flag along suggests downstream logic may use it.
